definitionEn: an impressive achievement that requires great skill, strength or courage
situation: Praising something remarkable that someone has achieved, especially through great skill, strength, effort or courage.

examples.text: Building the tunnel through solid rock was an extraordinary engineering [[feat]].
Running two marathons in one week was quite a [[feat]] for someone recovering from injury.
Translating the entire novel in three weeks was no mean [[feat]], even for an experienced translator.

texts: Landing the rocket booster upright was hailed as a remarkable [[feat]] of engineering.
Memorising the entire speech overnight was an impressive [[feat]] for a nine-year-old.
Keeping the family business running through the crisis was no small [[feat]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Feat — достижение, которое требует умения, силы или смелости. Простое везение — a stroke of luck, не a feat.

collocationTask.prompt: escaping the burning building was a ___ of pure courage
collocationTask.explanationRu: «Проявление отваги» — a feat of courage. Case, point и topic с courage в этом значении не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Climbing the north face solo in winter was a [[feat]] that few climbers would even attempt.
nuance.explanationRu: Feat — не просто достижение, а по-настоящему впечатляющий поступок, требующий силы, смелости или мастерства. Achievement — более общее слово, подходит и для скромных успехов.

reverse.text: Finishing the course on time was a small [[achievement]] she was quietly proud of.
reverse.explanationRu: Скромный, не особо впечатляющий успех — просто achievement. Feat подразумевает что-то по-настоящему выдающееся.

fixIt.text: Climbing the mountain without oxygen was an incredible [[heroism]] that stunned the climbing world.
fixIt.explanationRu: Heroism — обычно неисчисляемое качество («героизм»), не «поступок». Конкретное впечатляющее достижение — a feat.

reply.context: A friend says: "My grandmother just finished her first triathlon at seventy-five."
options: Wow, that's a real feat at any age!
Wow, she must be a real feat now!
One must acknowledge that constitutes a considerable feat.
reply.explanationRu: Feat — впечатляющее достижение, а не человек. Второй вариант ошибочно называет саму бабушку feat, третий звучит слишком официально для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: relating to the belief that women should have the same rights and opportunities as men
situation: Describing books, ideas, movements or people that support equal rights and opportunities for women.

examples.text: The novel is often studied as an early [[feminist]] text, questioning the limits placed on women's lives.
She describes herself as a proud [[feminist]] writer, tackling gender inequality head-on in every book.
The magazine ran a series of [[feminist]] essays about the gender pay gap.

texts: Her latest book takes a strongly [[feminist]] view of fairy tales.
The film festival dedicated a whole evening to [[feminist]] cinema.
Their coursework included several classic [[feminist]] essays from the 1970s.

badCollocation.text: she wore a very [[feminist]] dress to the gala
badCollocation.noteRu: Feminine — «женственный» (о внешности, стиле). Feminist — про равноправие женщин; платье не может быть feminist.

collocationTask.prompt: the 1970s saw the rise of the ___ movement
collocationTask.explanationRu: Движение за равноправие женщин — the feminist movement. Feminine — «женственный», female — «женского пола», womanly — «по-женски»; здесь не подходят.

nuance.text: The play has been praised for its bold [[feminist]] message.
nuance.explanationRu: Feminist — о равноправии женщин (движение, идеи). Feminine — «женственный» (о внешности, манерах); message о равноправии не может быть feminine.

reverse.text: She has a very [[feminine]] sense of style, all soft colours and delicate fabrics.
reverse.explanationRu: Женственный стиль в одежде — feminine. Feminist здесь неуместно: оно о взглядах на равноправие, а не о внешнем виде.

fixIt.text: The magazine published a bold [[feminine]] essay arguing for equal pay.
fixIt.explanationRu: Feminine — «женственный». Эссе о равной оплате труда — a feminist essay, про равноправие, а не про женственность.

wordFormation.text: Historians describe her as one of the earliest [[feminist]] thinkers of her generation.

reply.context: A friend asks: "What's the new novel actually about?"
options: It's a feminist retelling of an old Greek myth, from the woman's point of view.
It's about a very feminist queen who loves pretty dresses.
It engages critically with feminist discourse surrounding patriarchal historical narratives, essentially.
reply.explanationRu: Feminist — про равноправие женщин и взгляд с их точки зрения. Второй вариант путает его с feminine, третий звучит как отрывок из научной статьи, а не ответ другу.

definitionEn: extremely fierce, violent, or intense in behaviour, force or feeling
situation: Describing an animal, attack, storm or feeling that is extremely violent, fierce or intense.

examples.text: The documentary shows a pride of lions launching a [[ferocious]] attack on a much larger buffalo.
A [[ferocious]] storm tore roofs off houses along the entire coast.
Competition for the internship was [[ferocious]], with over two thousand applicants for six places.

texts: The critic wrote a [[ferocious]] review that the director never forgot.
A [[ferocious]] dog guarded the junkyard at night.
The two candidates fought a [[ferocious]] battle for every last vote.

badCollocation.noteRu: Ferocious — свирепый, яростный, обычно про угрозу или силу. Широкую, доброжелательную улыбку называют a broad или warm smile.

collocationTask.prompt: the two firms are engaged in ___ competition for market share
collocationTask.explanationRu: Перед competition нужно прилагательное — ferocious. Ferocity — существительное, fiercely и ferociously — наречия.

nuance.text: The [[ferocious]] storm uprooted trees and tore off roofs across the whole village.
nuance.explanationRu: Ferocious — яростный, неистовый по силе, может описывать даже стихию. Aggressive — про поведение живого существа с явным намерением; про шторм так не говорят.

reverse.text: His [[aggressive]] driving nearly caused an accident on the motorway.
reverse.explanationRu: Агрессивная манера вождения — aggressive driving. Ferocious здесь избыточно: оно скорее про ярость, а не про манеру поведения за рулём.

fixIt.text: The critics gave the film such a [[hard]] review that the director refused to read it again.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Жёсткая, разгромная рецензия» — a ferocious review. Hard с review в этом значении не сочетается.

wordFormation.text: The [[ferocity]] of the storm caught even experienced sailors off guard.

reply.context: A colleague says: "How competitive was the job market when you applied?"
options: Honestly, it was ferocious — hundreds of applicants for one role.
Pretty ferocious, yeah, everyone was really polite and supportive about it.
The labour market conditions could accurately be described as ferocious in nature.
reply.explanationRu: Ferocious — свирепый, крайне жёсткий (о конкуренции). Второй ответ противоречив, третий звучит слишком официально для разговора с коллегой.

rewrite.original: The competition to get into the programme was extremely intense.
rewrite.frame: Competition to get into the programme was ____.

definitionEn: an inner quality of strength, courage or character that shapes how someone behaves
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «внутренний стержень, сила характера» (moral fibre); буквальное значение «волокно» (пищевое, текстильное) не рассматривается.
situation: Talking about someone's inner strength of character, especially their honesty and courage under pressure.

examples.text: It takes real moral [[fibre]] to admit you were wrong in front of the whole team.
Losing everything and starting again at fifty showed the sheer [[fibre]] of the man.
The coach questioned whether the young players truly had the [[fibre]] to cope with relegation.

texts: Standing up to the whole board alone took real [[fibre]].
It takes [[fibre]] to keep training every morning when no one is watching.
The interviewer said she wanted to see some [[fibre]] before offering the job.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Действовать на нервы» — get on somebody's nerves. Fibre — не «нерв», а «стержень характера» или (в другом значении) «волокно».

collocationTask.prompt: it takes real moral ___ to admit you were wrong
collocationTask.explanationRu: «Сила характера» — moral fibre. Fabric, material и texture — про ткань или физическую структуру, к характеру не относятся.

nuance.text: Admitting the mistake publicly took real [[fibre]], not just good luck.
nuance.explanationRu: Fibre — сила характера, стойкость. Muscle — физическая сила тела; признание ошибки требует не мышц, а морального стержня.

reverse.text: You need serious [[muscle]] to move a piano up three flights of stairs.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь нужна физическая сила — muscle. Fibre относится к силе характера, а не к мышцам.

fixIt.text: It takes real [[muscle]] to admit you were wrong in front of your whole team.
fixIt.explanationRu: Muscle — физическая сила. Признать ошибку публично требует не мышц, а морального стержня — fibre.

reply.context: A colleague says: "The new intern actually told the boss his numbers were wrong, in front of everyone."
options: Wow, that took some real fibre.
Wow, he must eat a lot of fibre.
One could argue the intern demonstrated commendable moral fibre in that instance.
reply.explanationRu: Fibre — стержень характера, смелость. Второй ответ обыгрывает буквальное значение (пищевые волокна), третий звучит слишком официально для разговора с коллегой.

definitionEn: to dishonestly change facts, figures or a situation to gain an advantage
senseNote: Здесь — неформальное «подделывать, мухлевать» (с цифрами, отчётами); значения «нервно теребить что-то» (fiddle with something) и «играть на скрипке» не рассматриваются.
situation: Talking informally about someone dishonestly changing numbers, records or a result to gain money or an advantage.

examples.text: The accountant was sacked after he was caught [[fiddling]] the company's expense reports.
Two officials were arrested for [[fiddling]] the results of the local election.
He'd been quietly [[fiddling]] his tax returns for years before anyone noticed.

texts: Rumours suggest the manager used to [[fiddle]] the till at closing time.
Auditors are trained to spot employees who [[fiddle]] their overtime hours.
It's surprisingly easy to [[fiddle]] small amounts on an expenses claim without anyone noticing.

badCollocation.noteRu: Fiddle (в этом значении) — подделывать цифры, отчёты, результаты. Мнение нельзя fiddle: change your mind или opinion.

collocationTask.prompt: he was caught trying to ___ his expenses
collocationTask.explanationRu: Подделать отчёт о расходах — fiddle your expenses. Fumble — «неуклюже уронить», meddle — «вмешиваться», muddle — «запутать».

nuance.text: Investigators discovered that the manager had [[fiddled]] the sales figures before the audit.
nuance.explanationRu: Fiddle — подделать нечестно, в свою пользу. Adjust — нейтрально «подправить»; перед аудитом менеджер явно жульничал, а не просто adjusted цифры.

reverse.text: We simply [[adjusted]] the schedule slightly to fit everyone's holidays.
reverse.explanationRu: Небольшое, честное изменение расписания — adjust. Fiddle подразумевает нечестность, обман, чего здесь нет.

fixIt.text: It later emerged that he had [[adjusted]] his expense claims for years to cover his gambling debts.
fixIt.explanationRu: Adjust — нейтральная правка. Раз речь о сокрытии долгов, значит человек мухлевал — fiddled his expense claims.

reply.context: A friend says: "Apparently our old landlord used to add fake repair costs to everyone's bills."
options: Seriously? So he was fiddling the bills the whole time?
Seriously? So he loves fiddling around the house?
Indeed, it appears the landlord was fiddling the invoices in a fraudulent manner.
reply.explanationRu: Fiddle — мухлевать, подделывать цифры. «Fiddling around the house» значит просто «возиться, копаться» — другое значение. Третий вариант звучит слишком официально и избыточно для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: It turned out he had secretly changed the numbers on his tax return.
rewrite.frame: It turned out he had secretly ____ his tax return.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Подделать налоговую декларацию» — fiddle your tax return.

definitionEn: extremely strong, intense or determined, especially in competition or feeling
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «крайне сильный, ожесточённый» (о конкуренции, споре, преданности); буквальное значение «свирепый» (о животном, нападении) не рассматривается.
situation: Describing competition, opposition, loyalty or criticism that is extremely strong, determined or intense.

examples.text: Competition among airlines on this route is [[fierce]], so tickets are unusually cheap.
She remains a [[fierce]] critic of the government's housing policy.
Despite their arguments, the sisters share a [[fierce]] loyalty to one another.

texts: The two companies are locked in [[fierce]] competition for the same contract.
He's a [[fierce]] defender of free speech, whatever the cost.
There was [[fierce]] resistance to the new parking charges from local shopkeepers.

badCollocation.noteRu: Fierce описывает конкуренцию, критику, споры, преданность. Сильную головную боль называют a severe или splitting headache, не fierce.

collocationTask.prompt: the two rivals fought a ___ battle for the title
collocationTask.explanationRu: Перед battle нужно прилагательное — fierce. Fierceness — существительное, fiercely и ferociously — наречия.

nuance.text: Competition for university places has become [[fierce]] in recent years, with far more applicants than spots.
nuance.explanationRu: Fierce — крайне ожесточённый, интенсивный. Tough — просто «трудный, непростой»; при таком резком росте числа заявок нужен более сильный fierce.

reverse.text: The exam was [[tough]], but most students still managed to pass.
reverse.explanationRu: Просто трудный экзамен — tough. Fierce здесь было бы слишком сильным словом: обычно оно про конкуренцию, критику или преданность, а не про сложность теста.

fixIt.text: Competition for the last places on the course became [[hard]] as the deadline approached.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Hard competition» так не говорят: нужно fierce (или stiff/tough) competition.

wordFormation.text: The champion defended her title [[fiercely]], refusing to give up a single point.

reply.context: A colleague says: "How's the race for the department head position going?"
options: Honestly, it's fierce — three really strong candidates, all pushing hard.
It's fierce, yeah, everyone's being really relaxed and easy-going about it.
The contest for the position may be characterised as notably fierce at present.
reply.explanationRu: Fierce — крайне ожесточённый, напряжённый. Второй ответ противоречив, третий звучит слишком официально для разговора с коллегой.

definitionEn: a person who writes, directs or produces films, especially as a profession or art
situation: Talking about someone whose job or art is writing, directing or producing films, especially documentaries or independent cinema.

examples.text: The [[film-maker]] spent three years living with the tribe before completing her documentary.
Local [[film-makers]] complained that the festival only ever invites big-name directors.
As an independent [[film-maker]], she has to raise every penny of her budget herself.

texts: The award went to a young [[film-maker]] making her first feature.
As a [[film-maker]], he's drawn again and again to stories about migration.
The city has become a magnet for every kind of independent [[film-maker]] you can imagine.

badCollocation.text: the famous [[film-maker]] who starred in the movie
badCollocation.noteRu: Film-maker — режиссёр или продюсер, тот, кто создаёт фильм. Актёра, снявшегося в фильме, называют an actor или a film star, а не a film-maker.

collocationTask.prompt: she is best known as a documentary ___
collocationTask.explanationRu: Профессия — a documentary film-maker. Film — само существительное «фильм», filming и filmed — формы глагола to film, а не человек.

nuance.text: As a [[film-maker]], she controls everything from the script to the final edit, not just what happens on set.
nuance.explanationRu: Film-maker — более широкое слово: человек, который создаёт фильм в целом (пишет, снимает, монтирует). Director — конкретно режиссёр, отвечающий за постановку на площадке.

reverse.text: The [[director]] shouted "action!" and the cameras began to roll.
reverse.explanationRu: Команду «мотор!» на площадке даёт именно director, а не film-maker в общем смысле.

fixIt.text: She's a rising young [[actress]] known for her documentaries about rural poverty.
fixIt.explanationRu: Actress — актриса, играющая роли. Тот, кто снимает документальные фильмы, — a film-maker.

reply.context: A friend asks: "What does your cousin actually do for a living?"
options: She's a film-maker — she's made a couple of really good documentaries.
She's a film-maker, always the lead actress in every scene.
Her professional occupation is that of a film-maker, as previously mentioned.
reply.explanationRu: Film-maker — тот, кто снимает фильмы, необязательно актриса. Третий вариант звучит слишком официально для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: to move gradually into or out of a place, or to slowly become known, in small amounts
senseNote: Здесь — «постепенно распространяться, просачиваться» (о новостях, людях); буквальное значение «фильтровать» (жидкость, воздух) и «отбирать» (кандидатов, контент) не рассматриваются.
situation: Talking about news, rumours or people that move gradually, in small numbers, into or out of a place or group.

examples.text: Rumours of the takeover began to [[filter]] through the office by lunchtime.
Tourists slowly [[filtered]] into the square as the parade drew closer.
Reports of the scandal have started to [[filter]] out despite the company's attempts to keep it quiet.

texts: News of the scandal will eventually [[filter]] down to ordinary shareholders.
Fans slowly [[filter]] out of the stadium long after the final whistle.
Complaints about the new system are already starting to [[filter]] up to senior management.

badCollocation.noteRu: Filter в этом значении — постепенно просачиваться. Мгновенное распространение — spread instantly или break, а не filter.

collocationTask.prompt: the news slowly ___ through to the rest of the staff
collocationTask.explanationRu: Постепенное распространение новости — filter through. Explode, erupt и vanish описывают внезапные или обратные события.

nuance.text: Word of the layoffs [[filtered]] through the building well before the official announcement.
nuance.explanationRu: Filter — постепенно распространяться в целом, необязательно тайно. Leak — просочиться, обычно про секретную информацию, слитую кем-то намеренно; здесь просто естественное распространение слухов.

reverse.text: Someone in finance must have [[leaked]] the confidential salary figures to the press.
reverse.explanationRu: Намеренная утечка секретных данных конкретным человеком — leak. Filter — просто постепенное, безличное распространение информации.

fixIt.text: News of the merger slowly [[exploded]] through the building days before the official announcement.
fixIt.explanationRu: Explode — произойти внезапно, взорваться. Постепенное распространение новости по зданию — filter through.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Does everyone already know about the office move?"
options: Pretty much — the news has been filtering through all week.
Yeah, I filtered the news to everyone myself yesterday.
It is understood that pertinent information has been filtering through the organisation accordingly.
reply.explanationRu: Filter — постепенно распространяться само по себе, а не «сообщать кому-то» напрямую. Третий вариант звучит как официальный отчёт, а не разговор с коллегой.

rewrite.original: Rumours about the closure gradually became known throughout the company.
rewrite.frame: Rumours about the closure gradually ____ throughout the company.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Слухи постепенно распространились» — rumours filtered through/throughout the company.
